Comment: CloudLab c240g5 (scripts/cloudlab/profile.py: node0 the control node, node1 to node4 the hosts of n1 to n4): the plans of the Quake example, decided once on this cluster: the update experiment's four minor batches of the 2026-02 diff (b4x5), each followed by a round of Quake's maintenance as a major epoch (internal/update/quake.go), every round saved by the runner as quake-plan-<k>.json.gz in the results, for the runs of experiment.wiki-c1024-kmeans-cloudlab-gpu-quake.json to run again ("Quake": {"Plan": FILE}; internal/update/quakeplan.go). Decided here, not on the lab server: a plan runs only on the state it was decided on, and the batches' inserts go to their nearest head by float distances, which this control node's router and the lab server's compute differently in the last bits (builds for their own CPUs): a vector nearly as near to two heads goes either way (the lab server's plans met list 428 with one posting more here, 2026-11-27). Quake's parameters: its Wikipedia configuration's (wiki.yaml: window_size 10000, refinement_radius 50, split_threshold_ns 250, delete_threshold_ns 500000, enable_delete_rejection false) and one refinement iteration, as its paper runs it (§7.2), the rest its defaults. The rounds' windows: the entries' last 2,500 client queries each (QuerySample), 10,000 in all. The entries chain at once (TriggerTimeSeconds 120-123: each runs to its end before the next) and may end after the load (600 s), which only fills the windows. On the 4-node warmup snapshot (experiment.wiki-c1024-kmeans-cloudlab-gpu-warmup-4.json), as the runs that replay the plans. nprobe 96, GraphHeadroom 10, UpdateLease and StageTimeout 120m: a round is decided under the lease, on this node's CPUs.
